title: BRICKSTORM Backdoor Investigation
description: Investigate a BRICKSTORM backdoor on a compromised target host.
outcomes: Identify malicious service running on the target host
Investigate persistence mechanism used by the malware
Detect malicious communication between the target and c2-server hosts

levels.title: Sandbox Overview
levels.content: Sandbox consists of three hosts: c2-server, target, and next-target. The c2-server is running a malicious backdoor named BRICKSTORM, which communicates with its C2 server over WebSocket using the DoH protocol.

levels.title: Access Level
levels.cloud_content: Connect to the cloud sandbox using provided credentials.
levels.local_content: Access the local sandbox via SSH as user cyrano.

levels.title: Identify Malicious Service
levels.content: Use netstat or ss command to list open network connections and active services on the target host.
levels.solution: Check for a service listening on port 4444 (e.g., `netstat -tuln | grep 4444`).

hints.title: First hint
hints.content: Look for a service with an unusual name or listening on an unexpected port.

hints.title: Second hint
hints.content: Check the process list for any processes related to the malware (e.g., `ps aux | grep brickstorm`).

levels.title: Investigate Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Look for modified system files, environment variables, or startup scripts that could indicate persistence.
levels.solution: Check the PATH environment variable on the target host (e.g., `echo $PATH`).

hints.title: First hint
hints.content: Investigate system files, such as /etc/profile or ~/.bashrc, for modifications related to the malware.

hints.title: Second hint
hints.content: Check the output of `env` for any unusual environment variables.

levels.title: Detect Malicious Communication
levels.content: Analyze network traffic, logs, or process listings to find indicators of compromise (IOCs) related to the BRICKSTORM backdoor.
levels.solution: Use tools like tcpdump or Wireshark to capture and analyze network traffic. Look for connections to IP addresses on port 8090.

hints.title: First hint
hints.content: Check the output of `netstat -an` for any connections to an unusual IP address or port.

hints.title: Second hint
hints.content: Investigate process listings for any processes related to the malware (e.g., `ps aux | grep brickstorm`).
